findings.title: Law-gate throw from record-turn! escapes turn error handling — one empty assistant reply kills the interactive REPL (and misreports single-turn success as exit 1)
findings.detail: write-artifact! is law-gated (infra/session.cljs:40-42, added in the previous review round): any artifact that fails law.session/valid-artifact? throws 'Refusing to persist an invalid session artifact: <malli explain>'. All three success-path callers invoke record-turn! OUTSIDE the try/catch that guards loop/run-loop: repl.cljs:130 (try only wraps lines 124-128), tui_repl.cljs:128 (try only wraps 121-126), agent.cljs:48 (try only wraps 43-47). Concrete reachable trigger: an assistant message with :content []. The turn-processor law requires [:content [:vector {:min 1} ...]] (packages/turn-processor/src/cljs/eta_mu/turn_processor/law/message.cljs:69), but the OpenAI client produces :content [] whenever a completion carries no text and no tool calls — accumulator->response omits :content when the accumulated text is "" (extern/openai.cljs:162-169), so openai-response->assistant-message yields (vec (concat [] [])) = [] (turn-processor/shape/message.cljs:151-154). An OpenAI-compatible server that streams only {"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"} (null/empty content — happens with local servers, refusal/content-filter responses) therefore: (a) in the REPL/TUI, unwinds the entire input loop and exits the process 1 with a raw Malli explain dump — a single odd provider reply terminates the whole interactive session, while every genuine run-loop failure is caught and the session continues; (b) in single-turn/piped mode, the turn already succeeded and streamed to stdout, yet the process exits 1 reporting a schema error, misreporting a successful turn as a failure. The same crash class applies to /clear (repl.cljs:118, tui_repl.cljs:114) and to any mid-session fs error (disk full), though those are less likely triggers. No test or e2e covers an invalid-but-produced message reaching the law gate: all mock servers send non-empty content, and the new tests only assert the happy-path append. Fix options: wrap the record-turn!/clear! calls in the REPLs so persistence failure logs and continues (conversation survives), or make the shape layer guarantee law-valid messages (e.g. emit a placeholder text part for empty completions).

findings.title: extern.os/homedir treats HOME="" as set, yielding a cwd-relative '.eta-mu' sessions dir
findings.detail: Line 9: (or (process/env "HOME") (.homedir os)). process/env returns the raw value whenever the var is set (extern/process.cljs:17 — when-let passes ""), and "" is truthy in ClojureScript, so HOME="" resolves to "" and eta-mu-home becomes (path/join "" ".eta-mu") — a directory relative to the current working directory. Sessions are then silently written into <cwd>/.eta-mu/sessions and are invisible to 'eta-mu session' run from any other directory. This is the twin of the ETA_MU_HOME='' case the previous review explicitly fixed via the (seq override) guard (infra/session.cljs:24-27); the new extern.os boundary reintroduces the same edge unhandled. Rare (set-but-empty HOME in minimal containers), but the repo has already legislated this class of bug once.

findings.title: session list preview can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair and embeds raw newlines from piped prompts
findings.detail: summary (line 84) truncates with (subs preview 0 (min (count preview) 60)). subs counts UTF-16 code units, so a 60-unit cut through an emoji/wide char leaves a lone surrogate that prints as U+FFFD in every 'eta-mu session' row. Separately, run-piped-input stores the entire trimmed stdin (including newlines) as the user message content (repl.cljs:157-160), so the first-user preview can contain literal newlines, breaking the one-line-per-session output of commands/sessions.cljs:19-23. Display-only corruption; no data loss.

result.reason: Every checkable element of the claim verifies against the actual code. (1) The law really does reject empty content: turn-processor law/message.cljs:69 requires assistant [:content [:vector {:min 1} assistant-content-schema]], and eta-mu law/session.cljs:27 embeds message/agent-message-schema in the artifact, so an assistant message with :content [] fails law/valid-artifact?. (2) The empty message is genuinely producible: extern/openai.cljs accumulator->response (lines 162-169) omits :content when accumulated text is "" and no tool calls exist, and shape/message.cljs openai-response->assistant-message (lines 151-154) then yields (vec (concat [] [])) = []; a chunk of {"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"} or null content takes exactly this path through apply-chunk! without error. (3) run-loop (infra/loop.cljs:207-209, 238-240) performs no law validation and returns the invalid assistant message as a successful turn, so the REPL try/catch (which only wraps loop/run-loop) never fires. (4) record-turn! sits outside that try in all three hosts at the exact cited lines — repl.cljs:130, tui_repl.cljs:128, agent.cljs:48 — and run-repl's outer try has only a finally, so the write-artifact! throw (session.cljs:40-42) unwinds the whole input loop into agent.cljs handle's catch, printing a raw Malli explain and exiting 1; in single-turn/piped mode the turn already streamed successfully yet the process exits 1. (5) Not grandfathered: infra/session.cljs and law/session.cljs are untracked new files and repl.cljs is modified in this card's uncommitted working tree; the law-gate was added in this card's own previous review round. (6) Not documented as accepted: card comment 69's accepted-with-rationale list covers eager create!, js/Date precedent, per-run overrides, and concurrency — never the law-gate-throw-escapes-the-REPL interaction. (7) Not minor: a single refusal/content-filter/local-server empty reply kills the entire interactive session while genuine run-loop failures are caught and survived — a disproportionate crash in the card's core delivered path (persistence in the turn loop), with zero test coverage of an invalid-but-produced message reaching the gate. The finding is real, in-scope, and promotion-gating.

findings.title: Same delivering commit adds raw js/process.stdout writes in eta-mu.infra.cli.repl, outside extern.*
findings.detail: DoD item 4 ('No raw Node/terminal interop outside extern.*') is satisfied by the card's own code (host.cljs requires only extern.terminal, host.cljs:10; tui_repl.cljs reaches the terminal only via eta-mu.terminal-ui.extern.terminal and input via eta-mu.extern.readline). However, commit 054dd55 — the commit delivering this card — also added new raw interop to the plain REPL: make-repl-emit writes streamed deltas via `(.write js/process.stdout ...)` at repl.cljs:71 and repl.cljs:81 (both are `+` lines in this commit's diff; the pre-existing `.on js/process.stdin` at :142/:145 predates it). eta-mu.extern.process exists as the designated boundary (its ns docstring: 'All direct access to `process` is isolated here') but exposes no stdout-write wrapper, and AGENTS.md's construction order states 'Nothing above extern touches a raw host object.' Under a card-scope-only reading of DoD 4 the item is met; under a whole-commit reading it is newly violated. A maintainer should decide whether the honest fix is a stdout write fn in eta-mu.extern.process used by make-repl-emit, or an explicit note on the card that DoD 4 covers only the host/tui-repl diff.

findings.title: 'thinking...' indicator is cleared by run-loop's own :agent_start event ~instantly, so it never stays visible during the actual model wait
findings.detail: The card's delivered-behavior claim is that the indicator 'shows between submitting a prompt and the first token/tool result'. It doesn't. tui_repl.cljs:120 renders ["thinking..."] and then immediately invokes loop/run-loop (line 122) with no intervening await. run-loop's first action is to emit :agent_start and :turn_start (packages/turn-processor/src/cljs/eta_mu/turn_processor/infra/loop.cljs:187-188) — synchronously at entry, before convert-to-llm and before stream-fn/first-token latency. tui-emit's guard (tui_repl.cljs:51-52) clears the indicator on ANY event, so :agent_start wipes it microseconds after it was drawn; the 'thinking...' bytes and the \r+ESC[K clear land in the same stdout batch. On a real model with multi-second time-to-first-token the user sees no indicator at all during the wait — the feature is effectively dead for its stated purpose. The pty verification on the card can't distinguish this (a mock SSE server responds instantly), and the eta-mu test can't catch it either: FakeTerminal's clear-line is a no-op (tui_repl_test.cljs:14), so the test only proves 'thinking...' was written to the buffer, not that it survived until first output. Fix direction: clear only on output-producing events (message_update with text, tool_execution_start, tool-result message_end, turn_end), not on run-loop bookkeeping events.

findings.title: tui-emit's `printed` counter is never reset on a mid-turn stream failure, so the next turn's reply silently loses its first N characters and its 'assistant ' label
findings.detail: `printed` is created once per REPL session (line 49) and is only reset at :turn_end when pos? (line 72). A mid-stream failure is reachable: the SSE reader's `.read` in pull-network! (packages/eta-mu/src/cljs/eta_mu/extern/openai.cljs:183) is unguarded, so a dropped connection after deltas were streamed rejects `.next`, throws out of loop/run-loop (loop.cljs:29), and lands in run-tui-repl's catch (tui_repl.cljs:123-126), which clears the indicator and prints 'Turn error:' but leaves `printed` at, say, 120. On the next user turn, message_update text shorter than 120 fails `(> (count text) @printed)` so nothing is written; once it exceeds 120, `(subs text @printed)` (line 61) drops the first 120 chars of the new reply and `(zero? @printed)` (line 59) is false so the 'assistant ' label is never printed. The corruption self-heals at that turn's :turn_end, but one reply is silently truncated. Fix direction: reset `printed` in the catch path, or scope it per-turn by resetting on :turn_start.
